{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOI30vQc8AAAABbX4U0A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm3E6zhE8UNU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm3E6", "number": 28, "title": "Document test and CI performance principles", "body": "## Problem

As features accumulate, test and CI work can grow through expensive integration checks, unconditional cross-products, repeated setup, duplicate triggers and obsolete runs. Contributors need a concise shared principle:

**Detect the required failures at the lightest appropriate layer, without redundant execution.**

Document this principle for this repository's development and review process. Preserve the confidence and required behavior provided by existing tests.

## Existing entry points

- [docs/development-flow.md](https://github.com/takahirox/webgpu-devtools/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md)
- [docs/review-guidelines.md](https://github.com/takahirox/webgpu-devtools/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md)

These were present when this Issue was prepared. Inspect their current versions and any existing testing/CI performance document before choosing the canonical location.

## Expected outcome

Keep one concise canonical statement in an appropriate existing testing/development document, or add `docs/testing-ci-principles.md` if no suitable document exists. Link to it from the existing development flow and review guidelines, with a short discoverable README/contribution link where appropriate. Avoid repeating the full policy in several files.

Adapt the following six principles to the repository's actual tooling and user-facing surfaces:

1. **Prefer the lightest meaningful test layer.** Cover calculations, branches and broad data combinations with fast unit/component tests. Use browser, renderer, emulator, real-model and end-to-end tests for behavior and boundaries that require those environments. Add tests that can catch a concrete defect; avoid tests that merely mirror the implementation.
2. **Choose combinations deliberately.** Avoid automatically multiplying every format, model, material, state, browser and deployment path. Use representative cases covering distinct processing paths, and exhaustive combinations where their interactions actually require them. Preserve required regressions and meaningful integration coverage when redistributing checks.
3. **Match validation to the change.** Distinguish documentation-only, UI, core/runtime and CI/build changes and their relevant checks. Give fast feedback, full regression validation and deployment/publication clear responsibilities and appropriate triggers. Keep mandatory pre-merge checks applicable to the change; record genuinely post-merge-only checks separately.
4. **Reuse work and eliminate duplicate execution.** Reuse builds, converted fixtures, downloads and other expensive setup with appropriate cache keys and isolation. Avoid running equivalent CI twice for the same revision through overlapping push/PR triggers. Stop superseded runs when safe, while preserving necessary deployment ordering. Consider independent parallel work with measured resource use rather than assuming more workers always help.
5. **Review test value and added cost together.** For new or expanded tests, ask what additional defect they detect, whether existing coverage already supplies that assurance, and what execution/maintenance cost they add. Pay particular attention to repeated fresh browser/renderer/compiler setup, large fixtures, long emulation loops and Cartesian-product growth.
6. **Maintain an execution-time budget.** Establish a repository-appropriate normal-CI target/baseline using available evidence, monitor growth, and investigate work exceeding the target. Separate elapsed feedback time, total runner/computation time and queue time. Revisit the validation structure and duplication when it grows; retain meaningful assertions and required coverage.

Include this review question, or an equivalent concise formulation:

> Does this change provide sufficient confidence with the lightest appropriate validation, without redundant execution?

## Integration and scope

- Read the current repository guidance and applicable instructions before editing. Reuse existing useful testing/performance guidance and preserve justified project-specific conventions.
- Explain how the principles apply to the checks actually present here. If no CI or test commands are configured, say so accurately and describe how the principles apply to existing checks and future additions; do not invent commands or introduce CI for this Issue.
- Use an existing measured baseline/target if available. Otherwise explicitly leave it unmeasured or to be established during actual test/CI performance work. This documentation task does not require new benchmarking, a universal time limit, a runner purchase, or a new merge gate.
- Keep the canonical section/document short and actionable. A small review prompt/link is sufficient; do not create a second lengthy checklist or a generic testing framework.
- Use English for new documentation and follow the repository's existing development, review and merge conventions.

This Issue documents principles. Changes to workflow triggers, test selection, timeouts, worker counts, caches, test implementations, dependencies or application behavior belong in separately scoped implementation work.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] A discoverable canonical section/document records all six principles and relates them accurately to this repository.
- [ ] Development and review guidance link to the canonical statement, and review explicitly considers additional coverage, duplication and execution cost.
- [ ] The guidance preserves required correctness/regression confidence and distinguishes mandatory pre-merge checks, optional validation and genuinely post-merge-only work.
- [ ] No unsupported performance claim, invented tooling, arbitrary universal timing requirement or new benchmark/hardware/human-approval gate is introduced.
- [ ] Existing relevant guidance is preserved and reconciled; references, repository names and commands match the current repository.
- [ ] Check Markdown structure, links/anchors, consistency and whitespace (`git diff --check`) with available tooling, and review the complete diff including new files.
- [ ] The change remains documentation only, without new runtime tests, workflow/configuration changes, dependencies, frameworks or unrelated refactoring.

## Validation for this documentation task

Markdown/link/anchor/consistency/whitespace checks are sufficient. Full application builds, browser/emulator suites, performance measurements, hardware tests and deployed-site verification are not required solely to add these principles. Future changes to tests or CI must still run their own applicable checks.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.
